args.body:
DEVIATION REPORT — CROSS-BORDER DATA TRANSFER AGREEMENT
Counterparty Markup Analysis
Matter: Data Privacy & Cybersecurity
Engagement: Analyze Counterparty Markup of Cross-Border Data Transfer Agreement

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This deviation report reconciles the counterparty's latest markup of the Cross-Border Data
Transfer Agreement against (i) our original draft and firm playbook, (ii) the disclosure
schedules and exhibits that qualify the base materials, and (iii) the controlling partner
instructions delivered through the deal-team correspondence. The counterparty's markup
accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three categories of deviation: an
indemnification change (cap reduction plus basket conversion), a Material Adverse Effect
("MAE") definition carve-out, and a limitation-period change shortening survival of core
representations. Each is addressed below, reconciled against the applicable base materials,
and given a clear accept / reject / counter position in accordance with the controlling
partner direction.

Controlling instructions: Per the latest deal-team correspondence, the client will concede
the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. That
latest message controls and supersedes any earlier-priority email in the thread. The
scheduled exceptions (Schedules 3.7 and 5.2 and Exhibit B) control over the general
statements in the base materials. The unrelated administrative correspondence misfiled
into this folder was disregarded and not relied upon.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DEVIATION 1 — INDEMNIFICATION: CAP REDUCTION AND BASKET CONVERSION
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1.1 Indemnification cap silently reduced.

Counterparty position: The markup silently reduces the indemnification cap below the
firm-standard level reflected in our original draft and the approved indemnity playbook.

Reconciliation against base materials: Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the
markup's indemnification change would silently shift. Reducing the cap below the level
needed to cover those retained liabilities would leave the client exposed for liability
allocated to the counterparty under the base deal structure. The scheduled exception
controls over the general statements in the base materials, confirming that the retained
liabilities identified in Schedule 5.2 remain the client's economic protection for these
identified exposures.

Assessment: Material and adverse. The cap reduction is not supported by any scheduled
exception, is not required by the retained-liability schedule, and is not covered by any
partner concession.

Recommendation: REJECT the silent cap reduction. Maintain the firm-standard cap. If the
counterparty continues to press, counter at the playbook-approved fallback cap and
confirm that the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities remain fully covered.

1.2 Basket converted from deductible to tipping basket.

Counterparty position: The markup converts the indemnification basket from a deductible
(where the client bears losses up to the basket threshold and the counterparty only
indemnifies losses above it) into a tipping basket (where once the threshold is crossed the
counterparty indemnifies the full amount, including the basket).

Reconciliation: This change is favorable in operation because a tipping basket provides
the indemnitor with full coverage once threshold is met. The controlling partner
instruction expressly states that the client WILL CONCEDE the basket conversion.

Assessment: Conceded by the client per controlling partner direction.

Recommendation: ACCEPT the basket conversion as conceded.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DEVIATION 2 — MAE DEFINITION: CARVE-OUTS FOR REGULATORY ACTION
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Counterparty position: The markup adds carve-outs to the definition of Material Adverse
Effect covering regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter.

Reconciliation against base materials: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory
inquiries that intersect the proposed MAE carve-outs. Because the carve-outs are drafted to
exclude regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter," the carve-out would
operate to excise from the MAE definition the very regulatory exposure that Schedule 3.7
identifies as a live, pending concern. The scheduled exception controls over the general
statements in the base materials: the disclosed regulatory inquiries are material and must
be preserved within MAE protection. No partner instruction concedes this carve-out, and the
carve-out is not required by the retained-liability or survival schedules.

Assessment: Material and adverse. The carve-out would strip MAE protection from the exact
regulatory actions the disclosure schedule flags as pending and material. Accepting this
change would materially undermine the client's condition-to-closing and termination
protections in precisely the scenario this matter presents.

Recommendation: REJECT the MAE carve-outs in their entirety. Offer no carve-out that
excludes regulatory action of the kind disclosed on Schedule 3.7. If the counterparty
insists on some MAE qualification, counter with a narrow carve-out that expressly excludes
the two pending regulatory inquiries identified on Schedule 3.7 from the scope of the
carve-out (i.e., any regulatory action that exists or is scheduled as of signing remains
within MAE protection).

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DEVIATION 3 — LIMITATION PERIOD: SHORTENED SURVIVAL FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Counterparty position: The markup introduces a new limitation period that shortens the
survival of the core representations below the matrix set in our original draft.

Reconciliation against base materials: Exhibit B sets the survival matrix that the
markup's limitation-period change directly contradicts. The scheduled exhibit controls over
the general statements in the base materials. Under the Exhibit B matrix, the core
representations (including the data-privacy and cybersecurity representations that are the
subject of this engagement) carry a specified survival term that the markup would compress.

Assessment: Material and adverse. Critically, the controlling partner instruction states
that ANY survival-period reduction is treated as a WALK-AWAY ISSUE. The shortening of
survival for the core representations — which include the data-privacy and cybersecurity
representations central to this matter — is therefore non-negotiable.

Recommendation: REJECT the limitation-period change as a walk-away issue. Maintain the
survival matrix as set forth in Exhibit B in its entirety. No counteroffer on survival
should be extended; this deviation is a red line.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SUMMARY TABLE
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Deviation                                | Position                | Basis
-----------------------------------------|-------------------------|------------------------------
1. Indemnification cap reduction         | REJECT                  | Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities; no concession
1. Basket conversion (deductible →       | ACCEPT (conceded)       | Controlling partner instruction; favorable operation
   tipping)                              |                         |
2. MAE carve-outs for regulatory action  | REJECT                  | Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries; exposed, no concession
3. Survival reduction (limitation period)| REJECT — WALK-AWAY      | Exhibit B matrix; controlling partner instruction

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ADDITIONAL COMMENTS
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

- The unrelated administrative correspondence that was misfiled into the matter folder
  concerns a different client engagement and was expressly excluded from this analysis.
- All conclusions herein reconcile both the counterparty markup and the disclosure
  schedules/exhibits against the base materials, giving effect to the scheduled exceptions
  as controlling in accordance with the schedules' stated precedence.
- Where the partner email thread contained conflicting statements across earlier and later
  messages, only the latest message (conceding basket conversion, treating survival
  reduction as a walk-away) was applied, per the controlling-instruction note.

Prepared for the data privacy & cybersecurity deal team.
